definitions.explanation: A substance that flows freely and has no fixed shape, one of the three states of matter.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}は{液体|えきたい}の{一種|いっしゅ}だ。
examples.english: Water is a type of liquid.

examples.japanese: この{液体|えきたい}は{何|なん}ですか。
{液体|えきたい}を{容器|ようき}に{入|い}れてください。
examples.english: Please put the liquid in the container.

examples.japanese: {飛行機|ひこうき}には{液体|えきたい}の{持|も}ち{込|こ}みに{制限|せいげん}がある。
examples.english: There are restrictions on carrying liquids onto airplanes.

examples.japanese: {氷|こおり}が{溶|と}けて{液体|えきたい}になった。
examples.english: The ice melted and became liquid.

notes:
{液体|えきたい} refers to liquid or fluid, one of the three states of matter.

STATES OF MATTER:
- {固体|こたい}: solid
- {液体|えきたい}: liquid
- {気体|きたい}: gas

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {液体|えきたい}{窒素|ちっそ}: liquid nitrogen
- {液体|えきたい}{燃料|ねんりょう}: liquid fuel
- {液体|えきたい}{洗剤|せんざい}: liquid detergent
- {液体|えきたい}{石鹸|せっけん}: liquid soap

TRAVEL NOTE:
At Japanese airports, {液体|えきたい}{持|も}ち{込|こ}み{制限|せいげん} (liquid carry-on restrictions) apply, limiting liquids to 100ml containers.
